clue.text: Fish in sea given drug, swimming with huge power

indicators.note: letters that are swimming move about freely, so the fish, sea and drug are mixed up together

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish out in the ocean has been doped and now swims with enormous strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' scrambles PERCH, SEA and DRUG together; 'in' and 'given' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine fitted with a forced-induction blower is boosted to great power, and figuratively anything so boosted is extra powerful.

clue.text: Person watching abridged version of Poltergeist claiming little bit short

indicators.note: to claim is to take in and hold, so the shortened ghost wraps around the other piece
an abridged version is cut short, so the ghost word loses its final letter

parts.note: a poltergeist is a noisy ghost, a spectre

indicators.note: short means the small particle word is missing its last letter

parts.note: an atom is a tiny amount, a little bit

explanation.surface: A shortened cut of the horror film Poltergeist has lost a small scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Poltergeist was a Spielberg production, in keeping with the theme, but here it is just a ghost; 'abridged version of', 'short' and 'claiming' do the trimming and wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks on at an event, such as a match, is an onlooker or viewer.

clue.text: Whitish grey, a metal in The Color Purple

indicators.note: in places the article and metal inside the colour word

parts.note: plum is a deep purple colour, so the film title is read as the colour itself
taken as written
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A hue and a metal are spotted in the Spielberg film The Color Purple.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title, part of the puzzle's movie theme, is read literally as a purple shade, PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The precious metal's pale silvery colour gives its name to a light grey shade, as in platinum blonde.

clue.text: American plot has department devoid of leadership

indicators.note: without its leader means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a branch is a department or division of an organisation

explanation.surface: A US scheme involves a government department that has no leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a scheme, but here it is a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A large farm in the United States, a stretch of land for cattle, is a plot of land in the American sense.

clue.text: Eat everything, including salt, and enjoy yourself

indicators.note: including means the sailor is placed inside the eating-and-everything pair

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat it
all means everything
an old salt is a sailor, an AB or able seaman

explanation.surface: Clear your plate, salt included, and have a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like seasoning, but it is a sailor: AB, able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a thoroughly good time.

clue.text: Market two films screened by opposite sides

indicators.note: screened by means hidden behind, so the films sit within the two sides

parts.note: right and left, R and L, are opposite sides
E.T. and A.I. are two Spielberg films

explanation.surface: Two movies are shown on screens at either end of a hall to market them.
explanation.walkthrough: E.T. and A.I. are both Spielberg films, in keeping with the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail goods is to sell them to the public, that is, to market them.

clue.text: Spot on end of nose needing operation after kiss

indicators.note: after places the operation piece following the kiss
end of picks the final letter of the word nose

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter
an act is an operation or deed

explanation.surface: A spot on the tip of someone's nose needs surgery after they kiss someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot on' reads as a blemish on the nose, but it is the definition, meaning precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British slang for precisely right, accurate.

clue.text: State-provided range

parts.note: Mass. is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A mountain range supplied by the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a mountain range.

clue.text: Sound decoration for fiddle

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for a decoration is heard rather than written

parts.note: a medal is a military decoration

explanation.surface: A pleasing ornament on a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like the instrument, but it means to tinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle with something is to interfere or tamper with it.

clue.text: Pack leader of female kangaroos bouncing back

indicators.note: bouncing back means the letters found are read in reverse order
of means the letters are taken from within these two words

explanation.surface: The leader of a mob of female kangaroos hops backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A pack of kangaroos is not what is meant: the pack is of Cub Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the title of the adult leader of a Cub Scout pack, after the wolf in The Jungle Book.

clue.text: Probation: message about it breaking through

indicators.note: about means the message word goes around the rest

parts.note: a note is a short message

indicators.note: breaking means it splits into the word for through

parts.note: via means by way of, through
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about probation, with something breaking through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' makes VITIA; 'about' then wraps the message word around it. The definition is the trial period of a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is the trial period served by a novice before taking vows, a probationary stage.

clue.text: Inebriate, Charlie leaving from the Highlands

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for Charlie departs from the word

parts.note: the Highlands are in Scotland, so from there is Scottish
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drunk called Charlie leaves the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inebriate' here is the adjective meaning drunk, not the noun for a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sottish means like a sot, habitually drunk, so it matches the adjective sense of being intoxicated.

clue.text: A film trailer for movie

parts.note: taken as written
a film is a thin layer or haze, a mist
a trailer is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A trailer for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' and 'trailer' sound like cinema, but they are a haze and an advert; the movie is Spielberg's Amistad.
explanation.definitionFit: Amistad is a 1997 Steven Spielberg film, fitting the puzzle's Spielberg theme.

clue.text: Beginning of fast: a tad suety, possibly?

definitions.text: Beginning of fast: a tad suety, possibly?

indicators.note: beginning of picks out the first letter of the word fast

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: As Lent begins, someone is feeling a little stuffed with suet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles TAD SUETY into TTUESDAY. The whole clue doubles as the definition: the pancake day of feasting is how the Lenten fast begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, the pancake feast eaten up just before Lent's fast begins, so the day ushers in the fast.

clue.text: Following offence, criminal trials left

indicators.note: following puts the rearranged letters after the offence word

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: After a crime, the criminal trials were abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb, departed, but it is the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinistral means on or towards the left side, or left-handed.

clue.text: Comic actor, film star in audition?

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the star's word is said aloud

parts.note: a film star is a screen idol

explanation.surface: A comedian auditions to become a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audition' looks like a casting session but means when heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle of Monty Python is a comedian and actor.

clue.text: School in Close Encounters blows up

indicators.note: in places the school inside the encounters word

parts.note: close encounters, romantic meetings, are dates
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school in the film Close Encounters explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Close Encounters of the Third Kind is a Spielberg film, but here it is read as dates.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to explode, to blow up.

clue.text: In Lincoln, key turning up for case

indicators.note: in places the reversed key word inside the Lincoln name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: key means vital, essential

explanation.surface: In the city of Lincoln, a key turns up for a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Spielberg made the film Lincoln; here Lincoln is just ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, expressing means or separation.

clue.text: Survivor cut in Duel gets shiner

indicators.note: in puts the cut survivor inside the duel word

parts.note: a duel is a fight

indicators.note: cut means the survivor word loses its last letter

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past

explanation.surface: In the film Duel, the sole survivor gets a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Duel was Spielberg's first feature; 'shiner' reads as a black eye but is anything that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow given off by a hearth's flames is something that shines, a shiner in the literal sense.

clue.text: Get down ridge below peak of Fuji

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts the ridge piece under the first letter
the peak is the top, so the first letter of the mountain's name

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf or ridge

explanation.surface: Descend a ridge below the summit of Mount Fuji.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' suggests descending, but here it means grow down, soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird fledges when it acquires its feathers, its down.

clue.text: Infant school's last break, 1:10 curiously

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so these letters are put in a strange new order
last picks the final letter of school

parts.note: taken as written
1 is I in Roman numerals, and 10 is ten

explanation.surface: An infant school's final break of the day comes at ten past one, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' mixes the L ending 'school's', BREAK, I and TEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle biter is jokey slang for a small child, one low enough to nip at ankles.

clue.text: Poker like this, expected to win

definitions.meaning: the ... poker is a tall flowering plant, as well as a heated fire iron
a strong favourite is described as a ... one

explanation.definitionFit: A poker is red hot when heated in a fire, and a red-hot favourite is the one tipped to win.

clue.text: A vehicle: it rolled forward!

parts.note: taken as written
a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: rolled means turned over, so the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A vehicle rolls forward, someone shouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Avanti is Italian for forward or come in, used as an exclamation urging someone on.

clue.text: Video devoid of content in things like Gremlins develops

indicators.note: in places the emptied video inside the goblin word

parts.note: gremlins are mischievous sprites, like elves

indicators.note: devoid of content means emptied, so only the outer letters of video remain

explanation.surface: A video of the film Gremlins has nothing on it, and develops.
explanation.walkthrough: Gremlins was produced by Spielberg; here gremlins are mischievous little beings, like elves.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually.

clue.text: Hiding in wardrobe, a handsome Caribbean charmer

indicators.note: hiding in means the letters are tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A handsome Caribbean charmer hides in a wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: A charmer sounds like a handsome lover, but it is one who casts charms.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of folk magic or sorcery practised in the Caribbean, and also its practitioner, a casting of spells.

clue.text: Academic gained by working on novel, finally

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the gained word follows the final letter
finally picks the last letter of the word novel

parts.note: money earned is gained by working

explanation.surface: An academic was paid for finishing work on a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned describes a scholarly person or work, erudite and academic.

clue.text: See 18 across
Jumper something with hole, back grimy originally

parts.note: a golf green is something with a hole in it
fro means back, as in to and fro

indicators.note: originally picks out the first letter of grimy

explanation.surface: A sweater with a hole in it, its back originally grimy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, but it is a leaping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The green frog is a North American frog, a leaping amphibian.

clue.text: Opener enthusiastic about collecting runs

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the runs letter goes inside

parts.note: to be into something is to be enthusiastic about it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An opening batsman is keen on piling up runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture suggests an opening batsman; the opener is the start of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening part of a song or speech.

clue.text: Notes passed on correction of line in Jaws

indicators.note: in places the rearranged line inside the jaws word

parts.note: to jaw is to chatter, so jaws means chatters

indicators.note: a correction alters something, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A corrected line of dialogue in the film Jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaws is Spielberg's shark film, but here it is a verb, chatters; 'correction of' rearranges LINE into INLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain letters are messages each recipient is urged to copy and forward to others.
